full_judgment:
4111 court of the Assistant judge, Dhaka impleading the petitioners including the opposite party Nos.2 and 3 as defendants praying for a decree tier declaration that the letter no.75/92 dated 6.8.92 removing the plaintiff from the post of assistant Teacher of Kadamtala Purbu Basaboo Uchha Biddalaya was illegal, void and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff and also for a decree for mandatory injunction against the defendants for her reinstatement in service and payment of back wages allowances of Government benefits etc. The suit was transferred to the court of the Assistant Judge, Dohar, Dhaka and was re-numbered as Title Suit no.27 of 

 4. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record found that service of the plaintiff was not made permanent after expiry of her probationary period. The trial court further found that the plaintiff was appointed as a temporary junior teacher and on expiry of her probationary period there was nothing to show that she was confirmed in the service. The trial court also found that re-presentation was pending before the Appeal and Arbitration committee of the Board and in such fact when the matter was pending in a forum, there could not to be any cause of action for the suit. The trial court also found that the plaintiff did not mention the amount of back wages and other benefits but brought the mandatory injunction without payment of adveloren court fees and thus the suit was not maintainable. Accordingly by judgment and decree on 8.2.99 the trial court dismissed the plaintiff's suit. 

 5. The plaintiff then preferred Title Appeal No.I21 of 1999 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka who heard the said appeal found that the plaintiff was appointed as temporary junior teacher on 5.3.88 and that her probationary period was 2 years, she was allowed to continue in service continuously for 21/2 years more and therefore relying on a decision reported in 29 DLR 104 held that continuation in service of the plaintiff would amount her confirmation in the service. While holding the aside view, the lower appellate court also referred to a paragraph from the decision of the Appellate Division without mentioning the citation that when the probationary continues in this service even after the expiry of the probationary period and further receives increments of salary-discharging him from service after the expiry of probationary period is illegal. Since the plaintiff was not discharge it would mean she was confirmed in the service. The lower appellate court further found that the approval of the authority of Recognised Non-Government Secondary School Teacher (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka) Terms and Conditions of service Regulations 1979 provides that Boards approval in case of removal of a teacher is mandatory. In the present case the plaintiff’s removal was not approved as required in the said Regulation and as such removal from service was not legal. The lower appellate court also considered certain rules of the Regulation and found that before imposing any penalty of dismissal or removal the matter must be examined by the Appeal and Arbitration committee and approved by the Board. This was admittedly not done in the case of the plaintiff. The lower appellate court accordingly held that the letter Ext.4 dated 1.8.92 removing the plaintiff from the service is illegal and without jurisdiction. The lower appellate court also considered Ext.5, which is re-presentation made by the plaintiff to the Board of Education. The lower appellate court also considered Ext.7 which is the decision of the Board whereupon it has been clearly stated that the Appeal and Arbitration committee of the Board in their meeting dated 30.12.92 and 15.7.93 found that the allegation brought against the plaintiff was not proved and there was irregularity in the matter of taking section against the plaintiff and the plaintiff was directed to be reinstated in service with her salary on condition of her tendering unqualified apology to the Headmaster in writing with assurance that she would carry out all the orders of the Administration of the school in future and it was further ordered that the Board should be informed within 10 days from the date of issue of the letter the compliance of the letter allowing plaintiff to join her service. The lower appellate court has found even after the Ext.7, the school authority did not allow the plaintiff to join her service. The lower appellate court has considered Ext.10, a letter. of the School Inspector to the Head Master of the School inviting his attention to the decision of the Appeal and Arbitration committee of the Board of Education and asking the Headmaster to allow the plaintiff to join her service and even after such letter which mentioned that in default to the compliance of the decision containing in the letter Exit.10, action would be taken against the Headmaster of the school in accordance with law and necessary step would be taken to withdraw the government benefits to the school but even then the plaintiff was not reinstated in her service. On consideration of all other evidence on record the lower appellate court disagreed with the decision of the trial court and by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.7.99 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the plaintiffs suit without arrear salary, allowance and other Government and non-Government benefits.
